quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
You must wait for the police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: When driving to a place you do not know, what should you do?

options.text: Use road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
You only need to know the general direction.
Always take the shortest route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your route before you start driving. Check a map of your destination before you leave.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must let the other go first?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When is it okay to use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to destinations. They help drivers find their way.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: Besides using turn signals, how can other drivers know you are going to turn?

options.text: By your vehicle position and eye contact.
By the angle of your wheels.
By how slow you are going.
By the actions of the car behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: By your vehicle position and eye contact.
questions.explanation: Use your vehicle position and eye contact to show other drivers your intentions. Always use turn signals in addition to these actions.

questions.question: When can you park on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: If you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only if there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if there is an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the shoulder of a freeway except in an emergency.

questions.question: The traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection unless you cannot stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection unless you cannot stop safely.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If stopping safely is not possible, drive carefully through.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks right away as fast as you can.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to let any train pass first.
Speed up to beat any train coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to let any train pass first.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let trains cross first. Do not cross until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: When you exit a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well ahead of time. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you don't block the intersection.

questions.question: What is most important about speed when driving around curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit entering the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn, so you must reduce speed to stay in control.

questions.question: What best keeps you safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting to reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see behind your vehicle when backing. Before you sit down to drive, walk to the back of your vehicle to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
It does not require extra caution from drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in place or moving, such as vehicles that stripe lines, mow, or remove snow. Work zones have orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left since the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means you can turn in that direction.
It means a green arrow is coming next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow light. Slow down and get ready to stop when you see it.

questions.question: If you need to stop fast and your vehicle does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Pump your brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car stops quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: A stuck accelerator will keep your vehicle moving even if you take your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully—move it just enough to stop the engine, not to lock the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and pull off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: You see a school bus stopped on the highway with red lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Stop before reaching the bus and wait until it starts moving again.
Stop before reaching the bus and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
Stop before reaching the bus and proceed after all children board or exit.
Stop and wait until the bus leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before reaching the bus and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing, you must stop at least 30 feet away from it. Do not move until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change. This is the best way to check your blind spots.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves, so you should slow down.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and turn on your signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a minor accident, move it off the road if you can. Always identify yourself and help if someone is injured.

questions.question: When you cannot see as well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down whenever you have trouble seeing. This is the most important thing to do in poor visibility or bad road conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and give the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down at the intersection and be prepared to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Signal to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. You should signal other road users by using your turn signals when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn or emergency lights when needed.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Where should your car be after you complete the turn?

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn left onto a one-way street, complete the turn in the left lane. This is the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming cars may not see you pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully around cyclists.
